analysis:
The batch changes only golden test fixtures under libs/darkbloom-cluster/Tests/PlacementChecks/Golden/layouts/: gemma-4-26b-8bit.json, gemma-4-26b-qat-4bit.json and gemma-4-26b.json. Each is a single JSON line (line 1). The diffs I could see (qat-4bit fully, 8bit head only, gemma-4-26b.json patch excerpt only) make the same kind of change.

Changes seen:
- generationModes goes from [pipeline_v1] to [pipeline_v1, tensor_parallel_v1].
- New routedExperts object (128 experts, 8 selected, loadedBytes, tensorParallelDividedBytes).
- New tensorParallel object: 2 ranks, plan gemma4_heads_and_expert_channels_v1, reduction sealed_all_gather_sum_v1, float32 partials, per-layer divided/replicated byte counts.

These are test goldens, not runtime code. They do not touch the provider process, coordinator WebSocket, attestation, key custody, prefix cache (T-041 is the only definition supplied in detail) or fan helper.

The fixtures do describe a new tensor-parallel generation mode with sealed all-gather reductions between ranks. If the corresponding non-test source is in the same PR, a later pass should check that the per-hop sealing and authentication of partials is end to end, that rank peers are authenticated, and that the layout-derived resource bounds are enforced. Those checks are about the source and are not verifiable from these fixtures.

For the 8bit and gemma-4-26b.json files I saw only the head text or a truncated patch, so I could not confirm that every change there matches the qat-4bit change. No concrete security regression is visible in the supplied evidence. I raised needs_deeper_review because the implementing code is outside this batch.
